subject: Consolidated adapter spec: Pinecone / pgvector / S3 (next steps)
messages:
From: Amy Chen <amy@vectorforge.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: initial outreach - storage/vector consolidation

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

Thanks again for the intro last week. Quick context from our side: VectorForge runs a mixed deployment - most customers use Pinecone for cloud-based dense retrieval, but we have a sizable segment that needs an on-prem/air-gapped option backed by S3 + pgvector. Our product team wants a single adapter strategy so our ingestion and retrieval stack can be consistent across cloud and private installs.

Top asks:
- Can Redwood propose a \"consolidated adapter\" approach that covers Pinecone (managed), pgvector (Postgres + pgvector extension on S3-backed volumes), and an S3 cold-tier path (for large archives)?
- Security/residency constraints (we may need to keep raw embeddings on-premise for some customers).
- Ops model: who owns shard lifecycle, index rebuilds, and fallback behaviour when Pinecone pods are unavailable?

We've sketched a rough SOW and a network diagram (attached). Would like to review a technical spec from your side and set milestones for a joint pilot (VectorForge + Pinecone + Redwood). Peter at Pinecone is on-copy and is interested in co-engineering this.

Proposed times for a 45m working session: Thu 10/22 10:30-11:15 PT or Fri 10/23 09:00-09:45 PT.

Thanks,
Amy Chen
Head of Data Partnerships
VectorForge

Attachment: vectorforge_sow_draft.docx (docx)
Attachment: network_diagram.png (image)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Amy Chen <amy@vectorforge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Peter Liu <peter@pinecone.io>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Consolidated adapter spec: Pinecone / pgvector / S3 (next steps)

Hi Amy — really appreciate the clear ask and the diagram. Marissa, Sergio, and I talked this morning; we sketched a first-pass adapter spec and a proposed mutual action plan. See the attached PDF for the technical sketch (redwood_adapter_spec_v0.1.pdf). Key points up front:

- Architecture idea (high level):
  * Adapter layer inside Redwood routing that maps a single retrieval API to backend-specific drivers (pinecone-driver, pgvector-driver, s3-archive-driver).
  * Metadata-aware routing: tenant-level policy decides primary store (Pinecone or pgvector) and fallback rules (cold retrieval from S3).
  * Consistent schema for vectors + payloads; Redwood will normalize dimension and dtype at ingestion time.

- Operational responsibilities:
  * Redwood: implement adapter and run integration tests, provide caching and retry semantics, host the routing control plane for hosted customers.
  * VectorForge: provide test data, access to a staging S3 bucket for archive replay, and an on-prem pgvector instance for validation.
  * Pinecone: finalize API contract for index management and lease-based pod reservations for the pilot.

- Security / residency:
  * We can architect the adapter so that raw embeddings never transit Redwood-hosted storage for on-prem tenants — instead, agent pods can be deployed into customer VPC. We'll include encryption-at-rest and KMS integration in the spec.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Working session Fri 10/23 09:00 PT (45m) — technical walk-through and confirm API contracts (Jonas to host).
2) Redwood to deliver adapter RFC (v0.2) by Mon 10/26.
3) Joint pilot acceptance criteria & timeline: pilot start target Nov 15, 2026.

Can you confirm Fri 9am PT works? I've attached the RFC stub.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Director, Partnerships & Alliances
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_adapter_spec_v0.1.pdf (pdf)
Related: HubSpot deal 7654321

From: Amy Chen <amy@vectorforge.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Peter Liu <peter@pinecone.io>, s3-ops@vectorforge.com
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Consolidated adapter spec: Pinecone / pgvector / S3 (next steps)

Jonas — Fri 9am PT works for our team. A few clarifying questions ahead of the call so we can move quickly:

1) Dimension mismatches: we have legacy indices with mixed-dim vectors (128/256). Will Redwood's normalization support runtime upcasting or padding, or do we need to re-index?
2) Cold retrieval SLA: if we pull archive vectors from S3 (object-store), what's your expected latency envelope and how will caching be pre-warmed for the pilot?
3) pgvector + S3: our on-prem reference will use Postgres 15 with pgvector extension, but storage is an NFS mount backed by S3-compatible object storage. Any known limits (sharding, VACUUM costs) we should flag?

Peter (cc) — if Pinecone is comfortable with a co-engineered index lifecycle API (create/index/snapshot/restore) we can reduce our operational load.

Also attaching our SOC2 summary and the SOW draft for the partnership (already shared with legal).

Best,
Amy

Attachment: vectorforge_soc2_summary.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: vectorforge_sow_draft.docx (docx)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Amy Chen <amy@vectorforge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Peter Liu <peter@pinecone.io>
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Consolidated adapter spec: Pinecone / pgvector / S3 (next steps)

Thanks Amy — great questions. Short answers below and a proposed mutual action plan. I'll put the RFC v0.2 in the shared Drive by Monday morning.

1) Dimension mismatches: Redwood adapter will support runtime padding for legacy indices (pad with zeros to a tenant-configured dimension) for read/serve only; re-index recommended for model-conversion pipelines. We'll document behavior in RFC v0.2.

2) Cold retrieval SLA: target cold retrieval P95 of 1.5s for 1-10k vector fetches when cache is cold (pilot hardware assumptions documented). We'll also provide a pre-warm utility to seed the cache from S3 snapshots. Exact SLA to be agreed in the pilot acceptance criteria.

3) pgvector + S3 notes: we recommend using partitioned tables per shard and scheduled autovacuum with tuned thresholds. We will include a CLI tool in the adapter package to assist with shard rebalancing. Known trade-offs attached in RFC.

Proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP):
- 10/26: Redwood RFC v0.2 delivered (Jonas)
- 10/28: Legal / SOW redline window (VectorForge + Redwood) — VectorForge to return comments
- 11/08: Pilot infra ready (staging Pinecone index + staging pgvector + S3 bucket) — owners: Peter (Pinecone), VectorForge SRE
- 11/15: Pilot start

Attachments to follow: redwood_adapter_spec_v0.2.pdf, pilot-acceptance-criteria.xlsx (I'll upload Monday).

Please confirm MAP and whether we should route the SOW via DocuSign (we can send an initial stub to your legal contact).

Onward — Jonas
Director, Partnerships & Alliances
Redwood Inference
